qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Shearing of κ-carbides by leading dislocations produces APBs and generates a preferential glide path (glide plane softening), leading to planar slip bands and Taylor lattice formation.
Dislocations bypass incoherent (Nb,Mo,W)C particles via the Orowan mechanism; strengthening contribution 6.5 MPa for HR45.

Intergranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particles act as preferential nucleation sites for microcracks; strain/stress concentration partially alleviated by debonding of intragranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particles and microvoid formation. Intergranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particles virtually played no detrimental effect on toughness.

interface_notes.value: The HR45 sample (coarser grains) showed microbands only at higher strains; microbands were observed at εe = 0.2 in HR68 and HR82, indicating faster substructure development with finer grain size.

phase_evolution.value: κ-carbides with L′12-type structure were produced by spinodal decomposition and subsequent ordering reaction during fast cooling (water quenching) without a further aging process.

coherence.value: coherent; sheared by dislocations generating anti-phase boundaries (APBs)
incoherent; dislocations bypass via Orowan mechanism; strain/stress concentration at interfaces due to deformation discrepancy

slip_behavior.value: Predominant dislocation planar glide; planar slip bands refining with strain and evolving into microbands; Taylor lattice formed by intersection of two non-coplanar {111} slip traces. For HR45 the slip band spacing at εe = 0.1 was 296.40 ± 50.06 nm, refining to ~50 nm at higher strains.

source.reason: Section 4.1 and 4.2 describe the precipitate/matrix interfaces and dislocation interactions (κ-carbide shearing, (Nb,Mo,W)C Orowan bypassing), the ductile-fracture role of intergranular (Nb,Mo,W)C, and the formation of κ-carbides by spinodal decomposition during water quenching.

processing_steps_notes.value: The steel was fabricated using a high-frequency vacuum induction melting furnace.

processing_steps_notes.value: Hot-forged into billets with a thickness of 110 mm at 1150 °C and then air cooling to room temperature.
